title: Anthrobot motility onset follows a sigmoidal time course peaking around day 10

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anthrobot motility onset follows a sigmoidal time course peaking around day 10

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: After release from the matrix, the number of motile Anthrobots rises along a sigmoidal curve over three weeks, with the largest change in motility on day 10, and this rise reflects a morphological reorganization that exposes cilia on the surface.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: To characterize the temporal dynamics of motility initiation, we periodically (every other day) counted the number of motile spheroids for 3 weeks following dissolution and observed a sigmoidal motility profile with peak change in motility on day 10 (Figure 1C).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures”. Scope: NHBE-derived Anthrobots in vitro, first 3 weeks after matrix dissolution

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The curve shape and peak-change day have explicit statistical tests. Public counts and staining can address them, but the causal attribution to reorganization is less well resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit sigmoidal and alternative time-course models to bidaily motile-bot counts and test whether the maximal fitted slope occurs near day 10 while surface-cilia abundance rises.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public materials may omit bot-level longitudinal identities.

Cilia exposure and motility may be measured in different samples.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A motile-fraction time series and a cilia stain are enough, in principle, to test both the sigmoidal timing and the reorganization clause. The census is figure-only and held on request, and the cilia comparison does not sample the day of steepest change. Confirming or refuting the fitted time course requires the count table or a new time series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Count motile spheroids every other day for three weeks after matrix dissolution, fit the motile fraction against time, and ask whether the largest step falls on day 10 and whether external cilia increase on the same schedule. A sigmoidal fit with the steepest step at day 10, matched by cilia exposure, would support the time course; a linear rise, a different peak day, or motility without added surface cilia, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The every-other-day counts behind the sigmoidal plot are not deposited.

A curve fit to one cohort does not separate maturation from selective survival of motile bots.

Cilia staining is reported at day 0 and day 7, not at the day-10 step.

data existence: 0.24
